title: 2. Test whether search needs grasp-and-lift-aware selection
hypothesis: When pick-place success is sparse, ranking successful grasp-and-lift behaviour ahead of geometric goal progress selects more transferable controllers from the same rollout candidates.

prediction.rationale: Baseline is the unchanged phase-searchability selector applied to the identical candidate pool. A 10-point confirmation gain would identify candidate selection, rather than generation or additional search, as a pipeline bottleneck; sharing all search rollouts makes this inexpensive.

code_changes: scripts/compare_generation_modes.py (--research-mode pick-place-suite: shared controls, lift-aware selector, grounding table, two-phase counterparts)

falsified_by: The block-level paired 95% interval has an upper bound below +0.10. A zero-spanning interval is inconclusive; the resolving measurement is fresh-case paired success of the two selectors' winners over additional independent structure pools.

controls.note: control is the control pools, original (success, progress) selector; the metric is already treatment minus control

result.notes: Shared-control suite on pick-place-v2 (no seed bank): 12 gpt-6.1-sol structures (4 single-phase controls, 4 single-phase with a source-verified interface table, 4 two-phase), all valid first time (16 calls); each given 24-candidate independent rollout search on a 5-case probe (s3214) with lift recorded, winners confirmed on 30 fresh cases (s3215). 1800 episodes (1440 probe + 360 confirmation). Ceiling: 7 of 8 single-phase structures already succeed untrained (probe 1.0 with lift), 12-17 of their 24 candidates succeed fully, and every single-phase winner scores 1.00 on confirmation. MetaWorld's pick-place success is puck-to-target <= 0.07 m. R-020: +0.000 block-level [+0.000, +0.000] by block [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. Both selectors chose the same candidate in all four control pools, so the contrast is exactly zero; the lift selector had nothing to break.

verdicts.reasoning: Lift-aware minus original selector is +0.000 [0, 0] over four blocks: the upper bound is below the predicted +0.10, which refutes. It is a ceiling, not evidence that lift-aware selection is useless: every control pool already contained fully successful candidates and both selectors picked the same one, so success-first ranking never needed a tiebreak.
verdicts.next_experiment: Selection is not the bottleneck when the pool contains successful candidates; revisit only on a task where search pools are sparse in success.

verdicts.reasoning: Against the named baseline selector, paired_success_difference was 0.000 with a block-level 95% interval of [0.000, 0.000] [logs/pick_place_selector_ablation/summary.json]. The upper bound is below the predicted +0.10, meeting the stated refutation criterion; the tie is not an improvement [logs/pick_place_selector_ablation/summary.json]. Both selectors chose the same candidate in all four control pools, and every selected winner achieved 1.00 confirmation success [logs/pick_place_selector_ablation/results.json]. This refutes the predicted gain on these pools but does not settle the conditional hypothesis about sparse-success pools, because the tested control pools already contained successful candidates [logs/pick_place_selector_ablation/results.json].
